rows.why: Submitted the real /wallet-meta/{wallet} editor form on the commit-bound instance (tag=risk, color=red, note=row017-display-only-proof). After reload the same form returns tag=risk/color=red/note=row017-display-only-proof and ui_state.wallet_meta[wallet] holds exactly that row (persist), while live_config.json sha256 was byte-identical before and after (f199111a5bccf65acf4389df32867b0351c66ab53b22e28102528001f5a794fc) and the wallet does not appear in live_config at all (display-only). The assertion binds tag/colour/note specifically, so it would fail for a different row.

Add of an EXISTING wallet returned ok with exactly one key present for that address (dup_key_count=1) instead of a second record; then archive moved it to archived_wallets and out of wallets; then re-add returned ok, removed it from archived_wallets and restored the SAME record, evidenced by the archived_at timestamp (2026-10-19T08:41:43.372289+00:00) and the previously set fixed_notional=99.0 surviving the round trip - a freshly created record could not carry archived_at.

Route genuinely absent: HL_Live_Copy_Service.py as the WS/poll health producer. The isolated :8032 instance has no running engine (health text: "Stopped: the engine is not running (no engine status found)"), /api/live-ws-health returns enabled=false, wallets={} and the follower account is ACCOUNT_ADDRESS_UNAVAILABLE, so no per-wallet WS subscription, poll coverage or freshness can be produced or aged. Observed, not scored: a wallet set to LIVE is reported live_wallets=1 while subscribed_wallets=0, ws_subscription=NOT_SUBSCRIBED and no per-wallet block (send_block_reason=MASTER_REAL_ORDERS_OFF only) - this is the polling-mode path, so it neither proves nor disproves the WS-coverage block the row requires.

With 3 configured wallets (2 LIVE, 1 OFF) the bound DOM pill #lcWalletCount read exactly "3 / 10". Independent oracle: a direct read of /api/live-config returned 3 wallet entries. The count is derived from live-config only (tracked=Object.values(lcConfig.wallets).length) and the value discriminates this row (it changes with the configured set). Caveat recorded, not hidden: after all four source APIs were aborted the pill kept the last known "3 / 10" with no stale marker, while the status line went lc-bad.

#lcModeCounts rendered "Live wallets: 2 / Close-only wallets: 0 / Off: 1" for a config independently tallied as LIVE=2, CLO=0, OFF=1 from /api/live-config. The three counts are computed per mode in the browser from the config map, so a wrong mode tally would break the assertion.

Sending cell is bound to the master switch field specifically. Intercepting /api/live-audit-summary and setting only master_real_orders_enabled=true produced #lcBannerSending = "ON" / lc-green / title "real orders are being sent"; setting it false produced "OFF" / lc-grey / "sending is switched off (a choice, not a fault)"; the unmodified payload (master=false) also produced OFF. See also hdr03_master_false and hdr03_control_autosend_only in the same artifact: one field flipped the cell in both directions, and the untouched case did not.

Leader-feed pill bound to live_top_status.ws_status. Payload-controlled results: ws_status=WS_OK & ws_enabled=true -> "Websocket OK" / lc-green; ws_status=DEGRADED -> "Websocket degraded" / lc-amber; ws_status=POLLING & ws_enabled=false -> "Polling (normal)" / lc-grey; ws_status=OFFLINE & ws_enabled=true -> "Websocket degraded" / lc-amber. Unknown/offline never renders green, matching the row negative test. Same artifact keys ws_degraded / ws_polling / ws_offline.

FAIL on commit-bound instance only: the available probe fields do not prove a REAL ORDERS pill. Its broad any_REAL_ORDERS_text=true is unexplained by the artifact (no raw DOM/text match is recorded), while selector_lcRealOrders=false, runs.ui_core.hdr_loaded.hdr05_realorders=null, and the captured header_pills list contains no REAL ORDERS pill. The committed source at tested_commit 89b3bc7586bf328df336fc9ea721cee212617762 has no REAL ORDERS / lcRealOrders pill markup (the source grep yielded only the separate sending banner phrase). Therefore the text boolean is not sufficient evidence to overturn FAIL; this is not a fresh rerun, and the commit-bound artifact is a third surface, distinct from served hashes b45ff9af (:8031 /) and fad19d22 (:8023 /live-copy).

Status line reflects the load outcome in both directions. A normal Refresh left #lcStatus = "Loaded" with class lc-status lc-ok; after aborting all four sources (/api/live-config, /api/live-ws-health, /api/live-audit-summary, /api/global-controls) and refreshing, #lcStatus = "Failed to fetch" with class lc-status lc-bad; after un-aborting and refreshing it returned to "Loaded" / lc-ok. See runs.ui_core.failclosed.status and runs.ui_core.recovered.status.

Refresh performs exactly its own action: one click issued exactly the four expected requests (/api/live-config, /api/live-ws-health, /api/live-audit-summary, /api/global-controls - captured from the network layer, no others), completed in 5.05 s, set #lcStatus to "Loaded" and re-rendered #lcWalletCount. The same key records the error path where those requests fail and lcStatus turns lc-bad.

Global Controls toggle is a pure show/hide: first click set #lcGlobalControlsPanel aria-hidden=false and class "lc-gc-popover active"; second click restored aria-hidden=true and class "lc-gc-popover"; zero additional /api requests were observed across both clicks. Contrast with BTN-05, which writes config.

Add wallet button opens the modal it names: clicking [data-lc-modal="lcWalletModal"] set #lcWalletModal aria-hidden=false with class "lc-modal-backdrop active" and exposed exactly the add-wallet fields (wallet, mode, copy_mode, norm_base, fixed_notional); the modal own close button returned aria-hidden=true. No submit was issued, so no config write is claimed.

Global Controls close button performs only its own action: the popover was opened (aria-hidden=false), then #lcGcClose set it to aria-hidden=true. This is the close control specifically, separate from the toggle in BTN-02.

Save Global Controls persists the fields it owns and reports success. Opened the popover, set Max per-order notional=123.45 and Max daily loss=7, clicked #lcGcSave: #lcGcStatus = "Saved" / lc-status lc-ok, and the isolated config then reported max_order_notional_usd 123.45 (previously 99.0) and max_daily_loss_usd 7.0 while unrelated fields were untouched (max_total 1234.5, allowlist BTC,ETH, blocklist DOGE). Negative input -5 was clamped to 0.0 on persist rather than stored negative. Restored afterwards.
